issues.claim: The Microsoft guidance on DDD microservices recommends a rich model for a complex domain, but notes that for a simple enough CRUD microservice an anemic domain model is not an anti-pattern.
issues.problem: The generator admits it did not re-read the page. The fetched excerpt is truncated before the Rich versus anemic section and never shows this statement. It shows only Fowler's quoted definition and the warning about complex microservices with logic in service classes. I recall the page saying a simple CRUD service can be fine with data-only entities, but I cannot confirm the exact 'not an anti-pattern' wording. The same claim appears in locales.ru.explanation, and the Microsoft link is cited for it.
issues.suggestedFix: Paraphrase to what the page is known to say: for a very simple CRUD microservice or bounded context, data-only entities (in effect a persistence model) may be good enough and not worth the extra DDD patterns. Drop the words 'not an anti-pattern' unless the full page text confirms them. Apply the same change to the ru and en blocks.

issues.claim: The downside is that there is no mandatory shared skeleton that forces reuse: repetition has to be noticed and refactored
issues.problem: Bogard's excerpt names the downside as the team needing to understand code smells and refactoring. It does not name duplication. The text does not credit duplication to Bogard, so this is acceptable, but the wording could make the attribution clearer.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally add that Bogard's own caveat is that the approach assumes the team understands code smells and refactoring.
